key_insight: In laser–TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, laser power, welding speed, and current govern molten-pool flow, weld geometry, and arc behavior.
engineering_relevance: These parameter–response relationships can guide weld penetration, width, and arc-stability control when fabricating Invar molds for aerospace composites.
method: Numerical simulation of molten-pool fluid dynamics
High-speed photography of pool evolution and arc behavior
Parameter analysis: 5–6 kW laser power, 0.5–0.8 m/min speed, and 150–170 A current
evidence_signal: Within the studied ranges, higher laser power increased penetration and arc deflection tendency, higher speed reduced penetration and width, and higher current widened the weld and improved arc stability.
watch_item: The abstract reports trends but no quantitative simulation–experiment agreement; extrapolation beyond the studied parameter ranges requires validation.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
